title: What If You Stared at the Sun? You Wouldn't Feel It

scenes.text: What if you stared at the Sun? You wouldn't feel the damage happening.
Your retina has no pain sensors, so there's no warning. Doctors say injury can take as little as one to two seconds.
The condition is called solar retinopathy, a light injury to the retina.
Symptoms like a blind spot, wavy lines or blurry vision usually show up within about a day.
There's no treatment. Some people recover over time, but often only partly.
Photoreceptors don't regenerate. As one eye doctor puts it, once you lose them, you lose them.
